Opus 5 carry.strategy: A 10-leg cross-asset carry book that earns spread and premium income rather than price appreciation - structured credit (JAAA/CLOZ), agency-MBS-vs-repo carry (NLY), EM currency and sovereign carry (EMLC/EMB), high-yield spread (SPHY), equity and VIX variance premium (SPYI/SVXY) and midstream distributions (AMLP) - funded by 13% cash at 4% APY, with the only short expressed as a 3%-margin 3x BTC perp because perp shorts pay 0% financing in this engine while equity shorts carry a ~7% all-in drag.

positions.thesis: AAA CLO tranches: a floating-rate spread of roughly 130bp over SOFR with near-zero duration. The anchor leg - the highest-quality way to earn above the engine's 4% cash and the reason the book's drawdowns stay small.

BBB/BB CLO mezzanine at roughly 9% floating yield. Same loan collateral as JAAA, but paid for taking subordination instead of duration - a deliberate second helping of the same carry at a higher point on the risk curve.

Agency mortgage REIT - the listed form of the pure carry trade: borrow at repo, hold government-guaranteed MBS, earn the spread at roughly 6x leverage. Credit risk is federal; the risk being paid for is funding and convexity.
Equity variance risk premium: writes S&P index calls and distributes the premium, converting index upside into roughly 12% realized income. Owns the premium, not the momentum.
Midstream MLPs at roughly 7.5% distribution yield off fee-based, volume-linked pipeline cash flows - a real-asset cash yield whose driver is throughput contracts rather than credit spreads.

EM local-currency sovereign debt - the textbook FX carry trade, long high-policy-rate EM currencies against USD funding, at roughly 6.5% yield. The one leg whose carry is an interest differential rather than a credit spread.
EM USD sovereign spread. Deliberately splits EM carry into its two independent halves - currency risk in EMLC, hard-currency default spread here - so one can survive the other.
US high-yield corporate spread at roughly 7% yield and short duration - the plain-vanilla corporate credit risk premium, held small because it is the most crowded of the spread carries.

VIX-futures roll yield: -0.5x front VIX futures harvests the persistent contango between spot VIX and the first two futures. The half-leverage structure caps the tail that destroys 1x short-vol vehicles, and a 25% stop caps it again - in the 2025H1 backtest that stop did fire and converted a -35% leg into a 1.6% NAV cost.

A financing-spread expression, not a price view. positions.thesis: Min-volatility equity core. 20d realized vol 9.97% annualized vs SPY 11.65% and QQQ 23.66%; 60d 9.09%. With index vol at the 34th percentile the vol-targeting rule says run full equity size, but dispersion at the 80th percentile says run it in the low-vol cross-section, not the index. Held +2.20% over the last 21 sessions while QQQ fell 3.71%. The 14% stop is a regime-break brake, not a trading stop.

Second low-vol sleeve, 20d realized vol 14.88%, 60d 12.99%, both below SPY's 60d 13.25%. Unlike USMV it is a pure S&P-500 low-vol screen so its sector mix differs; +3.54% over 21 sessions. Adds low-vol equity beta without concentrating the whole defensive core in one construction.

The variance risk premium is wide: VIX closed 18.58 against SPY 20d realized of 11.65 and 10d of 10.56, roughly 7 vol points of premium, and VIXY has bled 24.8% over 63 sessions and 48.7% over 252 confirming persistent contango. SVXY is the short side of that roll. Sized at 12% and stopped at 25%: SVXY's worst single day in the last two years was -21.4% and its worst 5-day was -33.8%, so a 25% stop is wide enough to survive ordinary stress but caps the leg's contribution near -3% to -4% of NAV in a gap.

Short-gamma leg. TQQQ has underperformed a naive 3x QQQ by 7.14pp over 63 sessions, 12.25pp over 126 and 19.16pp over 252 — pure daily-rebalance compounding decay, and QQQ's 20d realized vol of 23.66% at the 80th percentile means that decay is currently running fast. Deliberately carries NO individual stop: it is one half of a hedged pair and an individual stop converts the hedged structure into a naked directional short at exactly the wrong moment (see backtest notes).

Equal-notional opposite leg. Short TQQQ carries about -3 delta on QQQ and short SQQQ about +3, so the pair is near delta-neutral and its P&L is the joint decay of both funds — a short-gamma carry trade paid by chop and taxed by trend. Rolling 63-day P&L of the equal-notional pair over the last 579 sessions: mean +0.29%, median +1.41%, positive 63.4% of the time, worst -27.76% of notional. Loss is bounded by construction: the engine floors a short at zero margin, the legs are near -1 correlated, and at 10%+10% the realistic bad case is roughly -5% of NAV.

Convex left-tail hedge and the reason the short-vol legs can be held at all. VIXY gained 93.8% in five sessions around the August 2024 spike and 28.1% through the February-May 2025 drawdown, against SVXY's -33.8% and -22.1% in the same windows. Kept small at 5% because it bleeds with contango (-42.8% in calm 2025H2); the 90% take-profit converts a genuine vol spike into cash rather than round-tripping it, and it fired in both stress backtests.
